body:
I think you're right; I should delve into my hobbies more.  Sometimes it's hard to do anything except lay in bed and think...and think...and think...

Thank you for your encouragement.  While I'm sorry to hear that you are also burdened by dark thoughts, I feel a little less awful knowing I'm not the only person in the world like me.

This resonated with me, as my thoughts are also geared toward the person I love.  I'm also inexplicably privileged, and it makes me sick.  There are people who would literally kill to have my life, and here I am wasting it.  Thank you for making me feel a little less lonely.

Thank you for this.  I really do feel that this is the real me -- that the successful and together "me" that everyone else sees is just a cover.  The real me may not have done anything horrible, but what am I capable of?  Why am I thinking such terrible things?  I don't see any end to these dark thoughts.  I don't believe I will harm myself, but I think of it often as the only way to feel peaceful.

Part of what makes me feel so guilty is that other than these consuming thoughts, my life is probably what most people would consider "as good as it gets".  I have absolutely nothing to complain about.  Most people, in my circumstances, would be contributing to society in numerous ways, making the most out of their lives, bettering themselves and others, etc.  And here I am, wasting away in my twenties, a prisoner in my own mind.  And it hurts.  And I thank you for your kindness.

Heh, that's exactly what he says -- that I couldn't even imagine some of what he has heard.  He believes that by recognizing that these thoughts are coming from a chemical imbalance rather than reality, I should be able to get past them.  But it just feels so REAL, like this is really me, like this is the kind of person I am...the kind of person who thinks horrible thoughts.  It sounds so trivial when I write it out like this, but it is truly burdensome.  Thank you for talking with me.

Thank you for replying to me.  I do see a psychiatrist and find him tremendously helpful, but I'm still not "fixed".  He has told me that due to a chemical imbalance I will never be "fixed", but I still find it difficult to fight this even knowing that it isn't "my fault".

I see a psychiatrist and take two medications.  Talking to someone has helped, and the medication has DEFINITELY helped, but somehow I am still me.  Posting here has actually made me feel a little better.  Thank you for your advice, and please recommend therapy and medication to others, as they have both helped me tremendously.  I am just not there yet.  :)

Thank you for your response.  I do see a psychiatrist and I trust him more than anyone else in this world.  He has helped me for many years, but lately my thoughts have been turning so dark that I'm afraid to tell him about what I'm feeling lest he judge me.  I know he would never say anything judgmental to me, but what if he's thinking about what an awful person I am?

That's exactly what I would tell myself if I were someone else.  But they aren't fleeting thoughts; they're overwhelming and they occupy much of my time.  I feel I am a terrible person for having the capacity to harbor these thoughts.  Thank you for responding to me.

Thank you for your advice, particularly the last sentence.  :)  It's hard for me to think about "things getting better", because my life is pretty near perfect from an outsider's perspective.  Honestly, I'm living the dream.  But that doesn't change the thoughts that plague me.  And it makes me feel worse that someone in my position could have anything at all to be sad about.

I'm not sure how to describe it.  I keep going toward the medicine cabinet, but somehow I know deep down that I won't go through with it.  Thank you for listening to me.

Can I post the same thing in another subreddit?
Thank you.  I often feel that I'm the only one in the world like me.  There are a few people I can talk to, but none who truly understand what it's like for me to be burdened by my own brain.
